title: Inside the top groups: every link, part 1 of 5 (groups 1 to 3)
question: For the twenty highest-ranked groups: who is linked to whom, how, and where can each link be checked?
finding: The twenty top groups hold 222 recorded links between 163 members (attached members included); this part lists links 1 to 60. The commonest kinds are pays (grant, contract or rent) (76), shares an officer or director (name match) (74), same street address (29).
how: One row for each link between two members of a top-twenty group, taken unchanged from the screen or record named in the source column. Within a group, links inside the core come first, then case-file links, payments, shared officers and addresses. Built on the graph described under “The linked groups”: organizations, firms, San Francisco addresses and people (officers, registered lobbyists and consultants, officials) joined by eleven kinds of recorded link, each with its source. Public bodies, banks, utilities, insurers, law and accounting firms, universities, hospitals, office buildings, and any node tied to more than 12 others by one kind of link were removed first. A person appears only on a rare full name, in a public role on file, with a second independent record for each tie, and is always a name match. A member is called a party only if the record of case outcomes lists it as one; being named in a case file is shown separately. Groups are the connected sets that remain, or the tightly linked cores of sets larger than 40.
limits: Being linked is not being involved: nonprofits share board members, buildings and auditors all the time, and San Francisco is a small city. A group is a place to look, ranked by how many independent signs sit inside it. Each row is one record, not a judgment: check it at the source named. Every row with a person is a name match on a rare full name and is not confirmed to be one person; the last column says in which public records the name is on file. A link drawn from a case file shows the level of the case file, not of the two members it joins. Shares an officer or director (name match): board members often serve several organizations, and affiliates share leaders as a matter of course. Same street address: nonprofit centres, landlords and tenants, and fiscal sponsors share buildings. Pays (grant, contract or rent): sub-grants and specialist contractors are how programmes are delivered. Lobbies or consults for: lobbying and permit consulting are registered and reported. Gives to the campaign of: campaign donations are reported, with limits on amounts. Gift to an official: gifts to officials must be disclosed and are capped. Payment at an official's request: officials must disclose charitable payments they ask for. Official holds a seat, income or investment tied to it: the question is whether it was disclosed and the official stayed out of the decision. Drawn together in a case file: a case file also names bystanders, victims and people who were cleared.
